newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-QUALITY GAP EVIDENT AS SPAIN'S OLD FIRM THRIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-QUALITY GAP EVIDENT AS SPAIN'S OLD FIRM THRIVE.

text.p: Spain's old firm gave a clear demonstration over the weekend of the gap between the multi-billion peseta giants and the more modest sides condemned to follow in their wake.
Real Madrid overran Real Sociedad 6-1 on Saturday, only to see arch-rivals Barcelona go three better by beating Logrones 8-0 on Sunday.
With over a goal a game, Barcelona's brilliant Brazilian striker Ronaldo has scored more than five other sides in the Spanish league on his own.
"Our principal objective is trying to keep up with the `grandees'," said former Real Madrid striker Alfonso Perez, whose goals have helped the more modest Real Betis climb to fourth place.

In an almost insulting display of superiority at Nou Camp, Bulgarian striker Hristo Stoichkov defied Barcelona team mates and orders from manager Bobby Robson by taking a penalty with the score at 4-0.
Stoichkov, whose return to the Nou Camp has been overshadowed by the exploits of Ronaldo, turned the game into a personal scoring contest with the Brazilian and his compatriot Giovanni.
The end result was two goals apiece for the three players, 70,000 happy home fans and Barcelona sitting on a two-point lead over Real Madrid at the top of the first division.
"They massacred us...there are really big teams and there are small ones -- and money makes the difference," Logrones goalkeeper Andoni Cedrun said.
Many neutral Spaniards felt Atletico Madrid's unexpected league championship triumph last season was just what the country needed after 11 years of domination by Spain's two most prestigious clubs.
Barcelona won the league title in 1985 and from 1991-94, while Real were champions from 1986-90 and again in 1995.
Real's own close season investment has taken time to produce results after opening games in which Croatian Davor Suker and Montenegrin partner Predrag Mijatovic failed to click.
But the Balkan strike pair have come good since then, and picked up five of their side's six goals against Real Sociedad.
"That's the way I like to play," said Real coach Fabio Capello, himself a multi-million dollar signing from AC Milan.
Meanwhile, in the remote farming town of Almendralejo, home of newly-promoted Extremadura, fans were celebrating their side's first points in the top flight after seven consecutive defeats.
Expectation surrounding the visit of Real Madrid later in the season is already intense in a town whose population of 25,000 would fit into the vast Santiago Bernabeu stadium four times over.
